subject: Geo-locked backups, TTL and lawful-hold flow — DPA redline questions
messages:
From: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@aurumhealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Questions: backups, TTL and onshore geo-lock language in DPA

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start reviewing the DPA with legal and infra, a few specific questions came up around backup retention and what you call ‘geo-lock’ for backups (i.e., ensuring backups are stored only in a customer-designated geography and not moved for disaster recovery without customer approval). Our counsel wants clear, slotted language we can present to the board.

Top items: 
- Can backups be included in the same residency guarantee as primary workloads, including onshore restore-only access?
- Proposed TTL on backups and whether snapshots are considered retained data under the erase/erasures clause.
- What the certified-erase timeline looks like for backups (we expect a maximum of 90 days for full certified confirmation after a deletion request).
- Legal hold exceptions: how are holds applied across regionally geo-locked backups and what notification windows do you provide when a lawful hold prevents erasure?

I attached a short spreadsheet with the questions and a copy of our standard DPA redline — can you take a pass and let me know which items are deal blockers vs. clarifications? We’re hoping to close the DPA review by next Friday.

Thanks,
Emma Jenkins
Head of Procurement | Aurum Health
emma.jenkins@aurumhealth.com
Attachment: Aurum_DPA_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: lauren.bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions: backups, TTL and onshore geo-lock language in DPA

Emma —

Appreciate the clear list. I reviewed the spreadsheet and looped in Priyom (security & compliance) and Marcus (platform) to draft concrete redline language and timing commitments. Quick summary up front: 

1) Geo-locked backups: yes — we can commit that backups for the customer environment are written to and restored from the customer-designated region(s) only, unless explicit, documented approval is provided for cross-region restore for DR. We propose an appendix clause that defines allowed exceptions and an approval flow.

2) TTL vs snapshots: snapshots are treated as retained customer data while discoverable; we propose a two-tier retention policy (active snapshot window + archival TTL) with maximum archival TTL configurable up to X days by contract.

3) Certified erasure: our standard SLA for erasure confirmation from backups is 60 days; that can be extended to 90 days in the contract with an explicit acceptance of limited operational windows for encrypted-media wipe.

4) Legal holds: holds will prevent erasure in both primary and geo-locked backups. We will provide notification within 48 hours when a hold is placed and weekly status updates until release.

I attached our suggested redline (Acme_DPA_Redline_v2.pdf) and a short playbook excerpt. Can you confirm whether Aurum will accept a 90-day certified erasure option as a contract-level toggle and whether your legal needs a 48-hour notification window or a shorter one? If acceptable, we’ll produce clean redlines for signature and route for DocuSign.

Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow 10:00–10:30am PT to walk through the exception flow; I can book if that works.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_v2.pdf (PDF, 127KB)
Attachment: redwood_backup_playbook.pdf (PDF, 95KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions: backups, TTL and onshore geo-lock language in DPA

Lauren / Marcus —

Thanks — below are suggested replacement lines for the DPA that map directly to Emma's points. I recommend we include the short appendix that Lauren referenced and put the toggles in the SOW so sales can flip between 60/90 day certified-erase windows.

Insert after Section 3.2 (Data Location):
"Backups (including snapshots and archived media) shall be stored in the customer-designated geography(ies) and shall not be replicated to a different legal jurisdiction for the purpose of routine disaster recovery without Customer's prior written consent. Emergency cross-jurisdiction restore operations are permitted only when Customer provides documented approval via the Approval Flow in Appendix B or when required by binding legal process; any such event will be logged and reported to Customer within 72 hours."

Insert into Section 4.5 (Data Deletion):
"Backups are considered Customer Data and subject to Customer's deletion requests. Upon receipt of a valid deletion request, Provider shall: (a) remove primary copies within standard processing windows; (b) initiate certified-erase procedures for backups and archived media and provide a certified erasure confirmation to Customer within the contractual window (standard: 60 days; optional: 90 days if elected in SOW)."

Legal-hold note:
"Provider shall prevent deletion actions on all copies (primary and backups) for the duration of a lawful or contractual hold. Provider will notify Customer within 48 hours of a hold being applied and will provide weekly status updates until release. The existence of a hold and the responsible legal authority shall be recorded in the audit log and made available to Customer for a period of 12 months following hold release."

Operational notes for Marcus: we will need an internal playbook entry for the 48-hour notification + weekly reporting and an audit log extract capability for holds. Marcus — can your team commit to those timelines and the per-hold audit export?

—Priyom

Subject: Re: Questions: backups, TTL and onshore geo-lock language in DPA — next steps

Emma —

Thanks for the patience while we put language together. Quick recap and next steps: 

- Geo-locked backups: clause drafted (see attached redline) — backups will remain in customer-designated geographies; cross-jurisdiction restores require documented customer approval except in binding legal emergencies (we will log and report any such event within 72 hours).
- TTL / snapshots: snapshots are covered as Customer Data; we propose the two-tier window with archival TTL variable by SOW.
- Certified erasure: default 60 days; Aurum may elect a 90-day certified-erase window in SOW.
- Legal hold/process: holds prevent erasure across all copies; Redwood will notify within 48 hours and provide weekly status updates. Per-hold audit exports available for 12 months after release.

If Aurum accepts the 90-day certified-erase option to be selected in the SOW and agrees to the 48-hour notification tempo for holds, we will finalize the clean DPA and send to DocuSign by end of day Monday. Otherwise flag any non-starters and we’ll iterate.

Proposed meeting: Monday 10am PT to finalize SOW toggle and sign-off. I’ll send the calendar invite if that works.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
